title: Dévissage des complexes ½ simpliciaux ∂ - parfaits et structures multiplicatives… (1975 ou 1976) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Page 65 continues the discussion of tensor structures on the categories of semi-simplicial (½-simplicial) objects 𝒫_* ⊃ 𝒬_* ⊃ … and their transported versions 𝒫, 𝒫^*, 𝒫^·.

Heading. The top line most likely says that the correspondence between 𝒫_* and 𝒫^* is compatible with ⊗. In modern terms, the equivalence (of Dold–Kan or duality type) between the semi-simplicial side and the cochain side respects the componentwise tensor product introduced on the previous page.

Definition. Grothendieck then sets up a general definition. Let 𝓑 and 𝓑′ be k-additive categories carrying a k-bilinear ⊗, together with associativity, unit and commutativity constraints satisfying the usual compatibilities. In modern language these are k-linear symmetric monoidal categories (Saavedra's 'ACU ⊗-catégories').

A 'multiplicative structure' on a k-additive functor F : 𝓑′ → 𝓑 consists of:
- a natural transformation u_{X,Y} : F(X)⊗F(Y) → F(X⊗Y), not required to be invertible;
- a map α : 1_𝓑 → F(1_𝓑′).

These must satisfy three compatibilities, each written out as a commutative diagram:
- the associativity hexagon (u composed with a^𝓑 equals F(a^𝓑′) composed with u);
- the unit square, F(δ^𝓑′_X)∘u_{X,1}∘(F(X)⊗α) = δ^𝓑_{F(X)}, 'et symétrique' for the left unit;
- the symmetry square, F(σ^𝓑′)∘u_{X,Y} = u_{Y,X}∘σ^𝓑.

This is precisely a lax symmetric monoidal functor.

How it is used. The next page draws the standard consequences:
- F(1) becomes a commutative ring object;
- F carries commutative monoids to commutative monoids;
- such functors compose, giving a 2-category of k-additive ⊗-categories.

Grothendieck then specialises to 𝓑′ = K, the k-linearised category of finite semi-simplicial sets. A k-linear functor K → 𝓑 is the same thing as a cochain complex C^· in 𝓑. A lax monoidal structure on that functor is offered as the right notion of a 'semi-simplicial multiplicative structure' on C^·. In effect this is a functorial cup-product structure à la Alexander–Whitney / Eilenberg–Zilber, built into the representing functor.

Purpose. The page serves the larger project: dévissage of ∂-perfect semi-simplicial complexes together with their multiplicative structures, for example the multiplicative behaviour of the Ψ^i decomposition from the previous page.
errors: Possible inconsistency about α. The text says 'isom.' 1_𝓑 → F(1_𝓑′), apparently partly struck out in the manuscript. Yet the next page concludes that F(1_𝓑′) 'devient un objet-anneau', which is only an interesting statement in the lax case, where α is not an isomorphism. The intended notion is therefore lax, with α a mere morphism.
The phrase 'et symétrique' leaves the left-unit diagram implicit. In the symmetric case it follows from the right-unit diagram together with the symmetry square, so nothing is lost.
Notation: the unit constraint is written δ rather than the usual r/ρ. This is harmless.

ideas.what: Definition of a multiplicative structure on an additive functor between ACU ⊗-categories: maps u_{X,Y}: F(X)⊗F(Y)→F(X⊗Y) and α: 1→F(1), compatible with the associativity, unit and commutativity constraints
ideas.usually_credited_to: Bénabou (1963-67), Eilenberg–Kelly (1966); in the ⊗-category setting Saavedra Rivano (1972, Grothendieck's student)
ideas.where_published: The framework appears in Saavedra Rivano, 'Catégories tannakiennes' (LNM 265), written under Grothendieck's direction; I do not know of a Grothendieck-authored publication containing it

ideas.what: Compatibility of the semi-simplicial/cochain correspondence with the componentwise tensor product
ideas.modern_name: monoidality of the Dold–Kan type correspondence (Eilenberg–Zilber / Alexander–Whitney)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Eilenberg–Zilber, Eilenberg–Mac Lane (1950s); Schwede–Shipley (2003) for the monoidal Dold–Kan correspondence

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a careful but standard write-out of the definition of a lax symmetric monoidal functor, already standard by 1975 (Bénabou, Eilenberg–Kelly, Saavedra). The only mildly interesting point comes on the next page: encoding cup-product structures on cochains as lax monoidal functors out of finite semi-simplicial sets. That idea is not on this page itself and is close to well-known later approaches (Day convolution, functorial E∞-cochains).
transcription_corrections: The first line probably reads '𝒫_* avec 𝒫^* est compatible avec ⊗' (the calligraphic P categories), not 'ρ_* avec ρ^*'.
In the unit diagram the diagonal arrow is labelled δ^𝓑_{F(X)} and marked as an isomorphism (≀); the vertical arrow F(δ^𝓑′_X) is likewise an isomorphism.
The phrase before 1_𝓑 → F(1_𝓑′) is 'et isom.' followed by a struck-out word. The ensuing 'qui soient compatibles avec les données d'ass., d'unité & comm.' is correctly rendered.
The page number 65 appears at the bottom left.
